payload.executive_summary: Deliver a monolithic, single-command CLI (O1) that converts a folder of Markdown notes into a static site with per-note pages, stable URLs, preserved Markdown formatting, backlinks, tags, and fully client-side search. Execution is planned as thin-slice, acceptance-test-gated milestones, with explicit early Human-in-the-Loop (HITL) resolution of the two blocking specifications (Q1 link syntax; Q2 tag format) and “secure-by-default” rendering/ingestion constraints to mitigate critical security risks (notably XSS and path traversal).

architecture_choice.rationale: O1 (monolithic single-command CLI with an in-memory build pipeline) best matches the branch goal of fastest time-to-first-value with minimal upfront framework design, while still supporting all MUST requirements (static output, per-note pages, backlinks/tags/search) via a straightforward sequential pipeline. This choice also keeps operational complexity low (one command, offline build) and aligns with thin-slice delivery where each increment is shippable and can be acceptance-tested before expanding scope.
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: C1 orchestrates a single build run: (1) C2 recursively discovers .md files under the input root, parses frontmatter and Markdown, extracts canonical metadata (title/slug) plus tags and internal links; (2) C3 consumes extracted links to build a forward-link graph, resolves targets to URLs, computes backlinks, and emits unresolved-link warnings; (3) C4 aggregates tags across notes and builds a tag→notes index for tag navigation; (4) C5 builds a client-side search index artifact from note titles and plain-text content; (5) C6 renders per-note HTML pages (injecting backlinks and tag navigation), plus home/tag/search pages, and writes static assets; (6) C7 provides in-browser search UI that loads the generated search index and navigates to note pages. All outputs are static files in the output directory.

exit_criteria: Q1 and Q2 are answered and recorded as the single source of truth for link + tag parsing (HITL approval).

decision_log.question: Which architecture option should be used for the initial delivery plan?
decision_log.choice: Adopt O1: a monolithic, single-command CLI with an in-memory build pipeline that generates the full static site in one execution.
decision_log.rationale: This minimizes upfront framework complexity and optimizes for speed-to-first-value while still supporting the required pipeline stages (parse, links/backlinks, tags, search, render) as sequential in-process steps.
alternatives_considered: O2 plugin-based custom core (more extensible but higher upfront design cost).
O3 Eleventy/SSG-based approach (faster templating/watch mode but adds dependencies and constrains internals).
O4 multi-tool pipeline with intermediate artifacts (modular but increases orchestration complexity for users).
what_would_change_this_decision: If extensibility/themes/plugins become a near-term MUST (strongly favor O2).
If large-scale search performance and watch mode are top priorities early (consider O3).
If independent toolchain evolution is required across stages (consider O4).

evidence_pointers.note: Branch B1 selected O1 (if present in branch_set artifact).

decision_log.question: What is the default security posture for Markdown rendering to mitigate XSS/content injection risk?
decision_log.choice: Default to safe rendering: do not allow raw HTML passthrough unless explicitly opted in; sanitize/escape as needed; and block unsafe URL schemes (e.g., javascript:) in rendered links/images.
decision_log.rationale: K3 is critical severity and the output is meant to be viewed by readers in a browser; a secure-by-default stance reduces likelihood of shipping an unsafe static site, and aligns with governance HITL triggers regarding unsafe rendering behaviors.
alternatives_considered: Allow raw HTML by default (high risk; requires strong sanitization and explicit acceptance).
Strip all HTML and all non-http(s) URLs unconditionally (safer but may break legitimate content; could be configurable).
what_would_change_this_decision: A stakeholder explicitly requires trusted raw HTML support and accepts/mitigates the risk with a sanitization plan and added security acceptance coverage.
The selected Markdown flavor/renderer cannot practically disable raw HTML; would require switching renderer or adding a sanitizer layer.

evidence_pointers.note: XSS/content injection risk and mitigation guidance.
HITL trigger for unsafe rendering without explicit mitigation.

decision_log.question: How should filesystem ingestion be constrained to prevent path traversal and unintended file inclusion?
decision_log.choice: Constrain ingestion to the declared input root, default to not following symlinks, and reject any resolved paths escaping the root; include an allowlist for input extensions (at least .md).
decision_log.rationale: This directly mitigates K9 (high severity) and preserves user trust by preventing leakage of local files into the generated static site output.
alternatives_considered: Follow symlinks by default (higher risk; could traverse outside root).
Allow all file extensions (increases accidental inclusion and disclosure risk).
what_would_change_this_decision: A stakeholder explicitly needs symlink following within the repository and accepts the risk with additional guardrails (e.g., symlink target must still be under root).
A future requirement adds support for additional content types beyond .md, in which case the allowlist would expand.

evidence_pointers.note: Path traversal/unintended inclusion risk and mitigation guidance.
Recursive discovery of Markdown files under user-specified folder.

decision_log.question: When and how should internal link syntax be implemented given the blocking open question (Q1)?
decision_log.choice: Treat Q1 as a hard gate: do not implement link extraction/resolution/backlinks until the supported internal link syntax is selected and documented; implement exactly the chosen syntax first, with any additional dialects (e.g., wiki-links) behind explicit configuration later.
decision_log.rationale: K1 is high severity and Q1 is blocking; premature implementation risks incorrect link graphs and broken navigation/backlinks. Gating avoids rework and reduces ambiguity-driven defects.
alternatives_considered: Implement both standard Markdown links and wiki-links immediately with heuristic detection (likely ambiguous and brittle).
Implement only standard Markdown links and proceed without stakeholder confirmation (may fail user expectations).
what_would_change_this_decision: Stakeholder provides a definitive link syntax decision and test examples (then proceed).
A requirement arises to support multiple link dialects concurrently; would require explicit resolution rules and stronger test coverage.

evidence_pointers.note: Blocking open question on Markdown/link syntax.
Risk from ambiguous/mixed internal link syntax.
Forward link detection requirement depends on a specified syntax.

decision_log.question: When and how should tag parsing be implemented given the blocking open question (Q2)?
decision_log.choice: Treat Q2 as a hard gate: do not implement tag extraction and tag navigation until the tag representation is selected and documented; implement deterministic parsing rules (including precedence/validation) exactly per the chosen convention.
decision_log.rationale: K2 is high severity and Q2 is blocking; tag completeness is a MUST metric (R20), so the format must be unambiguous for deterministic tests and reliable navigation.
alternatives_considered: Support both frontmatter and inline tags immediately with unspecified precedence (invites inconsistency).
Only support frontmatter tags and ignore inline tags without stakeholder confirmation (may not match user workflow).
what_would_change_this_decision: Stakeholder confirms a single tag convention and provides examples (then proceed).
A later decision mandates supporting multiple tag sources; would require explicit precedence and enhanced diagnostics.

evidence_pointers.note: Blocking open question on tag representation.
Tag extraction requires a specified convention.

decision_log.question: How will per-note URLs/slugs be generated to be stable and avoid collisions?
decision_log.choice: Generate URLs deterministically from the note’s path relative to the input root (minus extension), applying a single canonical normalization/encoding scheme; detect slug collisions during build and fail with an actionable error unless an explicit override is configured.
decision_log.rationale: Stable URLs are required (R4) and collisions are a known risk (K5). Collision detection prevents silent overwrites and unpredictable navigation.
alternatives_considered: Use only filename as slug (higher collision risk).
Auto-resolve collisions by adding numeric suffixes (can break stability across builds).
Use a hash-only slug (stable but less readable URLs).
what_would_change_this_decision: A stakeholder prioritizes human-friendly slugs independent of folder structure (would require slug frontmatter or mapping).
A hosting constraint requires different URL shapes (e.g., all pages flat).

decision_log.question: What search implementation approach should be used under the static-site constraint?
decision_log.choice: Generate a client-side search index at build time as static artifact(s) and ship a browser-only search UI that loads and queries the index without network dependencies; defer advanced search features and scale optimizations until expected scale targets (Q3) are clarified.
decision_log.rationale: R5 requires fully client-side search with no server runtime (static constraint). Deferring advanced features prevents scope creep while still enabling the R19 quality metric to be validated with a representative query set.
alternatives_considered: Add a server-side search backend (disallowed by static-site constraint).
Ship no search initially (violates MUST R5).
Implement advanced fuzzy/highlighting features immediately (scope risk; not required).
what_would_change_this_decision: If Q3 indicates very large corpora that exceed feasible single-asset indexing, require a chunked/lazy-loading index design.
If stakeholders require advanced search UX (R28) for MVP, reprioritize and accept added complexity/testing needs.

evidence_pointers.note: Assumption that in-browser search is acceptable.
Search index scale/performance risk and need for Q3 targets.
